themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crumbling
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 26 this week—a 324% increase from the 6.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting rapid deterioration of pavement, potholes, or curb conditions across Crown Heights/Prospect Heights that may be safety hazards or affecting mobility.
evidence: 26 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.34, 324% spike)
Pattern coincides with winter weather stress and heavy foot/vehicle traffic in dense Brooklyn neighborhood
Recurring budget request for street maintenance suggests this is chronic, now acutely worsening
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: photograph specific street segments with major damage; interview residents about safety concerns and commute impacts
DOT accountability angle: when was the last street resurfacing cycle in this district, and what's the backlog for repairs?

themes_detail.label: Dangling Street Signs—Safety Risk
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints surged to 7 this week compared to a 0.2 weekly baseline (2700% increase, z-score 15.59)—an extremely rare statistical anomaly indicating dangerous overhead hazards that could injure pedestrians and should be remedied immediately.
evidence: 7 dangling street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 average over prior 8 weeks (2700% spike, z-score: 15.59—highest z-score in dataset)
Extreme rarity of baseline (nearly zero complaints) makes this week's cluster highly anomalous and urgent
Overhead hazards pose direct safety risk to pedestrians, especially in dense urban neighborhood
reporting_angles: Visual/urgent angle: locate and photograph the dangling signs, document which intersections are affected, show proximity to schools or high-traffic areas
City response accountability: call DOT and 311 to find out how quickly these are being repaired; get timeline for citywide sign safety audits

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints jumped to 14 complaints two weeks ago—a 348% spike from the 3.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.73)—suggesting widespread mold, poor ventilation, or indoor pollutants affecting homes and buildings in the district.
evidence: 14 indoor air quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (348% spike, z-score: 11.73)
Converges with high heat/hot water complaints (3,839 over 90 days) and water leak complaints (416)—suggests moisture-related housing quality issues
Housing stock in Crown Heights includes older buildings prone to mold and ventilation problems; affects vulnerable populations (elderly, children, asthma sufferers)
reporting_angles: Health impact angle: interview residents with respiratory illness or mold exposure; consult public health experts on seasonal indoor air quality issues
Systemic housing angle: investigate how many buildings in the district have repeated air quality violations; tie to landlord accountability and housing standards

themes_detail.label: Asbestos in Buildings
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints tripled to 3 this week from a 0.5 weekly baseline (500% increase, z-score: 5.0)—indicating potential friable asbestos exposure in aging buildings, a serious carcinogen hazard requiring immediate remediation and investigation.
evidence: 3 asbestos complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Converges with 291 alteration permits filed in past 90 days—renovation activity may be disturbing asbestos-containing materials in older buildings
Asbestos is highly carcinogenic; exposure during renovation without proper containment poses severe health risk to residents and workers
reporting_angles: Investigation angle: obtain DOB records for the 3 asbestos complaints this week; identify which buildings, check if they have active renovation permits, and whether proper containment protocols were followed
Contractor accountability angle: interview EPA/asbestos removal experts on whether renovation boom in the district is creating compliance gaps

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints jumped to 27 two weeks ago—a 238% increase from the 8.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.54)—suggesting excessive revving, illegal exhausts, or aggressive driving patterns affecting residential quality of life.
evidence: 27 vehicle noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 8.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (238% spike, z-score: 5.54)
Builds on consistently high noise complaint volume: 1,085 residential noise complaints and 488 helicopter complaints over 90 days show chronic quality-of-life stress
Vehicle noise particularly acute in dense Brooklyn neighborhoods with major thoroughfares (Atlantic Ave, Nostrand Ave, etc.)
reporting_angles: Enforcement angle: talk to NYPD about traffic enforcement patterns; are illegal exhaust modifications being ticketed, and what's the citation trend?
Resident impact angle: interview affected residents about sleep disruption and stress; document specific problem intersections or times of day
